issues.legal_issue: An independent insolvency proceeding may continue despite an admitted winding-up proceeding unless the winding-up has reached an irreversible stage making revival impossible.
material_facts: A winding-up petition against the company had been admitted and a provisional liquidator had taken possession of its assets.
A financial creditor’s application under Section 7 of the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code was admitted while the winding-up proceeding remained pending.
A sale of mortgaged property by a secured creditor was subject to pending challenge, and other company assets remained with the provisional liquidator.
The winding-up proceeding had not reached a stage at which corporate death was inevitable or the process could not be reversed.
issues.conclusion: The Section 7 proceeding was independent of the winding-up proceeding and could continue; admission of the winding-up petition did not bar it.
issues.legal_principle: Sections 7 and 238 of the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code permit an independent insolvency proceeding, and the Code prevails over inconsistent company-law provisions. A winding-up proceeding should not prevent an effort at revival unless it has reached an irreversible stage. The Court relied on Swiss Ribbons (P) Ltd. v. Union of India, Jaipur Metals & Electricals Employees Organization v. Jaipur Metals & Electricals Ltd., Forech (India) Ltd. v. Edelweiss Assets Reconstruction Co. Ltd., Kaledonia Jute and Fibres Pvt. Ltd. v. Axis Nirman and Industries Ltd., and Action Ispat and Power Pvt. Ltd. v. Shyam Metalics and Energy Ltd. It rejected the argument based on Sections 446 of the Companies Act, 1956 and 279 of the Companies Act, 2013.

rule.if: appeal_challenges_insolvency_admission and independent_insolvency_application and not winding_up_irreversible

predicates.appeal_challenges_insolvency_admission: A party appealed an order admitting an insolvency application while a winding-up proceeding concerning the same company was pending.
predicates.independent_insolvency_application: A creditor initiated an insolvency proceeding that was capable of being considered independently of the winding-up proceeding.
predicates.winding_up_irreversible: The winding-up proceeding had reached a stage at which the process could not be reversed and the company’s death was inevitable.
predicates.insolvency_proceeding_may_continue: The independent insolvency proceeding may continue despite the pending winding-up proceeding.

issues.definition: When an appeal challenges admission of an independent insolvency application during a winding-up proceeding, the insolvency proceeding may continue if the winding-up has not become irreversible.

issues.legal_issue: A secured creditor’s sale of mortgaged property outside a winding-up proceeding does not, by itself, make the winding-up irreversible when the sale is challenged and other company assets remain under the liquidator’s control.
material_facts: A secured creditor sold mortgaged property outside the winding-up proceeding after obtaining possession from the provisional liquidator.
The provisional liquidator challenged the sale, alleging that it exceeded the secured property and was conducted at an undervalue.
Other assets of the company remained with the provisional liquidator for the purposes of winding up.
If the sale were set aside, the sold asset could return to the provisional liquidator.
issues.conclusion: The sale did not make the winding-up irreversible in the circumstances of this case.
issues.legal_principle: Under Action Ispat and Power Pvt. Ltd. v. Shyam Metalics and Energy Ltd., a winding-up proceeding is irreversible only when it has reached a stage that makes it impossible to set the process back. A secured creditor may stand outside winding up and realise its security; the Court relied on M.K. Ranganathan v. Government of Madras and the authorities following it, including Central Bank of India v. Elmot Engineering Co., Industrial Credit and Investment Corporation of India Ltd. v. Srinivas Agencies, and Board of Trustees, Port of Mumbai v. Indian Oil Corporation. The availability of other assets and the possibility that a challenged sale could be set aside meant that the sale did not establish irreversibility here.

predicates.winding_up_transfer_case: The issue arose in deciding whether a winding-up proceeding should give way to an insolvency proceeding.
predicates.secured_creditor_sold_collateral_outside: A secured creditor sold property covered by its security without selling it as part of the liquidator’s winding-up sale.
predicates.sale_is_challenged: A party to the winding-up proceeding challenged the secured creditor’s sale.
predicates.other_assets_remain_under_liquidator_con: The liquidator continued to hold other company assets for the winding-up process.
predicates.secured_asset_sale_not_irreversible: The secured creditor’s sale does not, on those facts, make the winding-up process irreversible.

issues.definition: In a winding-up transfer dispute, a challenged sale of secured property outside the winding up does not make the process irreversible when other assets remain under the liquidator’s control.

issues.legal_issue: Alleged non-disclosure of a pending winding-up proceeding does not defeat an independent insolvency application that otherwise meets the applicable requirements.
material_facts: The creditor’s insolvency application was alleged to have omitted the pending winding-up proceeding.
The insolvency application was an independent proceeding under the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code.
The insolvency tribunal had admitted the application, and the Court considered the application on its own statutory merits.
issues.conclusion: The alleged non-disclosure did not affect the determination of the independent insolvency application.
issues.legal_principle: A Section 7 application is an independent proceeding and must be determined on its merits under the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code. Once the requirements of Section 7 and the other applicable provisions are met, the discretionary transfer route in the fifth proviso to Section 434(1)(c) of the Companies Act, 2013 does not displace the insolvency tribunal’s jurisdiction. The Court relied on Jaipur Metals & Electricals Employees Organization v. Jaipur Metals & Electricals Ltd., Forech (India) Ltd. v. Edelweiss Assets Reconstruction Co. Ltd., and the other authorities establishing the independent character of insolvency proceedings.

predicates.independent_insolvency_application: A creditor initiated an insolvency application that is legally independent of a pending winding-up proceeding.
predicates.winding_up_non_disclosure_alleged: A party alleged that the creditor did not disclose the pending winding-up proceeding when making the insolvency application.
predicates.insolvency_requirements_met: The insolvency application satisfied the applicable requirements for admission.
predicates.winding_up_non_disclosure_does_not_defea: The alleged non-disclosure does not prevent determination of the independent insolvency application on its merits.

issues.definition: If an independent insolvency application meets its requirements, an allegation that the applicant omitted a pending winding-up proceeding does not defeat the application.
